away.name: Sebastian Cossa
away.news: Cossa made his NHL debut with the Detroit Red Wings last season, playing one game, but this season has been his first full-time exposure at the NHL level. The 23-year-old goalie has had some solid outings, but has been inconsistent between the pipes, posting a subpar 3.20 GAA and .855 SV% in five appearances (3-1-0). That said, he was solid in his most recent outing, saving 30 of 33 shots (.909 SV%) in a 4-3 overtime win over the Pittsburgh Penguins. The Mammoth enter Tuesday's game as -128 road favourites against a Toronto Maple Leafs team that is 1-2-0 in their last three games.

home.name: Sergei Bobrovsky
home.news: Bobrovsky's start in Toronto has been unencouraging, as he's been regularly outplayed by counterpart Anthony Stolarz, but he returns to the crease Tuesday. The 38-year-old Bobrovsky has allowed three or more goals in nine of 10 games this season and is coming off his worst performance so far, allowing five goals on 17 shots (.706 SV%) in a 5-4 loss to the Seattle Kraken. He has a 3.29 GAA, .885 SV%, and a 3-5-2 record.

away.name: Stuart Skinner
away.news: Skinner led the Jets onto the ice for warmups.

home.name: Jacob Fowler
home.news: Jakub Dobes had a breakout 2025-26 season, leading the Canadiens to an impressive playoff run, but his sluggish start to 2026-27 opened the door for Jacob Fowler, who hasn't backed down from the challenge. The 21-year-old Fowler has been sensational to start the 2026-27 season, posting an impressive 1.84 GAA and .932 SV% in eight games (7-1-0). He had a sluggish outing in his most recent game, allowing four goals on 29 shots (.862 SV%), but still helped secure a 5-4 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins. The Canadiens enter Tuesday's game as -186 home favourites against a struggling Winnipeg Jets team on a nine-game losing streak (0-7-2).

away.name: John Gibson
away.news: Gibson led the Red Wings onto the ice for warmups.

home.name: Andrei Vasilevskiy
home.news: Vasilevskiy led the Lightning onto the ice for warmups.

away.name: Tristan Jarry
away.news: Devon Levi was running away with the starting gig for the Oilers, but suffered a multi-week injury, opening the door for Jarry, who has excelled in his most recent opportunity. The 31-year-old Jarry has stopped 42 consecutive shots and recorded shutouts in his last two games. He has a 2.53 GAA and a .901 SV% in seven games this season (4-1-2). The Oilers enter Tuesday's contest as +138 road underdogs against a surging New Jersey Devils team that is 5-1-0 in their past six games.

home.name: Connor Hellebuyck
home.news: Despite missing training camp and the first three weeks of the season by choosing not to report to training camp for the Winnipeg Jets, Hellebuyck has been solid in limited action since joining his new team, the New Jersey Devils. The 33-year-old American goalie has allowed two or fewer goals in both of his starts (2-0-0), posting a 1.50 GAA and .923 SV%. The Devils enter Tuesday's action as -150 home favourites against the Western Conference-leading Edmonton Oilers, who have outscored opponents 12-1 during a three-game winning streak.

away.name: Joel Hofer
away.news: Since the season opener, the Blues have made it clear that Hofer is their go-to goalie. The 26-year-old Hofer battled adversity in his most recent outing, allowing four goals on 28 shots (.857 SV%), but still salvaged a 5-4 win over the Detroit Red Wings. Hofer has won four of his last five games (4-1-0), posting a 2.44 GAA and .925 SV%. The Blues enter Tuesday's action as slight +104 road underdogs against a New York Rangers team that has lost six of their last seven games (1-5-1).

home.name: Dylan Garand
home.news: After a season-ending injury to Igor Shesterkin, the Rangers were forced to rely on Garand, who performed admirably in early-season action. That said, the 24-year-old rookie has struggled in recent games, allowing 15 goals on 97 shots (.845 SV%) in his last four outings (0-4-0). Still, the Rangers enter Tuesday's outing as slight -115 home favourites against the St. Louis Blues, who are riding a two-game winning streak.

away.name: Jesper Wallstedt
away.news: Wallstedt has been busy with Filip Gustavsson (hip) sidelined and will return to the crease for the 15th time in Minnesota's first 17 games. The 23-year-old Swedish goalie has been outstanding to start the 2026-27 season, posting a solid 2.06 GAA and .920 SV% in 14 games (9-2-3). He was stellar in his most recent outing, saving 26 of 27 shots (.963 SV%) in a 5-1 win over the Washington Capitals. Minnesota enters Tuesday's contest as -179 road favourites against a Philadelphia Flyers team coming off a 6-3 win over the Utah Mammoth.

home.name: Dan Vladar
home.news: After allowing 15 goals on 105 shots (.857 SV%) in his first three games (0-3-0), Vladar has played better in recent weeks. The 29-year-old Czech goalie has helped his team record a point in five straight games (3-0-2), posting a 2.17 GAA and .910 SV%. That said, the Flyers enter Tuesday's contest as +161 home underdogs against a Minnesota Wild team on a five-game point streak (4-0-1).

away.name: Adin Hill
away.news: Hill led the Golden Knights onto the ice for warmups.

home.name: Arturs Silovs
home.news: Silovs has already matched a career high with two shutouts this season in just nine games, but has been wildly inconsistent. The 25-year-old Latvian goalie has allowed four or more goals in five of nine games (5-3-1), posting a pedestrian 2.98 GAA and .889 SV%. The Penguins enter Tuesday's outing as slight -110 home favourites against a Vegas Golden Knights team that played last night, losing 3-2 in a shootout to the Boston Bruins.

away.name: Jake Oettinger
away.news: The Stars have struggled offensively this season, but are off to a solid 8-5-1 record thanks to strong netminding from Jake Oettinger. The 27-year-old American goalie was solid in his most recent outing, saving 24 of 25 shots (.960 SV%) in a 3-1 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets. In his last 10 games (7-2-1), he has a dazzling 1.58 GAA and a .923 SV%. The Stars enter Tuesday's outing as slight -102 road underdogs against a Washington Capitals team coming off a 5-1 loss to the Minnesota Wild.

home.name: Logan Thompson
home.news: Thompson has quietly become one of the NHL's most consistent and reliable goalies over the past several seasons, coming off consecutive 31-win campaigns. That said, the 29-year-old goalie has been inconsistent at the start of the 2026-27 season. In his most recent outing, Thompson allowed four goals on 27 shots (.852 SV%) in a 5-1 loss to the Minnesota Wild. He has allowed three or more goals in five of his last eight games (4-4-0), posting a 3.04 GAA and .891 SV%. The Capitals enter Tuesday's game as slight -108 home favourites against a Dallas Stars team that has scored only six goals in its last three games (1-2-0).

away.name: Scott Wedgewood
away.news: Wedgewood's tremendous 2025-26 season, with a 2.02 GAA and .921 SV% in 45 appearances (31-6-6), was expected to earn him at least a timeshare in 2026-27, but he has struggled out of the gate. The 34-year-old goalie has only played four of 15 games for Colorado this season, posting an ugly 3.48 GAA, an .889 SV%, and a 1-2-1 record. In his most recent outing, he allowed six goals on 35 shots (.829 SV%) in a 6-2 loss to the Nashville Predators. Colorado enters Tuesday's game as -118 road favourites against a Columbus Blue Jackets team that has scored two or fewer goals in six of their past seven games (3-4-0).

home.name: Cam Talbot
home.news: Jet Greaves was expected to carry a heavy workload this season, but some rough outings have awarded Talbot some extra playing time. The 39-year-old Talbot was solid in his most recent outing, saving 29 of 32 shots (.906 SV%) in a 4-3 overtime win over the Philadelphia Flyers. He has a 2.83 GAA and .894 SV% in six appearances (3-2-0). The Blue Jackets enter Tuesday's game as +104 home underdogs against a Colorado Avalanche team that has outscored opponents 15-6 during a three-game winning streak.

away.name: Pyotr Kochetkov
away.news: Hurricanes Head Coach Rod Brind'Amour has rotated goalies almost evenly in recent seasons, but Pyotr Kochetkov's outstanding early-season performances have led him to deviate from the plan. The 27-year-old goalie returns to the crease on Tuesday for a fifth straight start. The 27-year-old goalie is coming off a 26-save shutout, his second of the season, in a 7-0 win over the Winnipeg Jets. The Hurricanes enter Tuesday's game as sizeable -196 road favourites against a Nashville Predators team coming off a 5-4 win over the Tampa Bay Lightning.

home.name: Juuse Saros
home.news: Saros has had consecutive disappointing seasons, finishing with a sub-.900 SV% the first two times in his career. He started the 2026-27 season on an encouraging note, but has struggled in recent games. The 31-year-old Finnish goalie has lost three straight (0-1-2), posting a 3.22 GAA and .892 SV%. The Predators enter Tuesday's game as +174 home underdogs against a 12-2-2, league-leading Carolina Hurricanes team riding a four-game winning streak.

away.name: Laurent Brossoit
away.news: Brossoit returned last season after nearly a two-year injury absence. The 33-year-old goalie has spent most of his time in the AHL since then, but is trying to make the most of an opportunity with a Ducks team that has struggled between the pipes. In his only game this season, Brossoit saved 20 of 23 shots (.870 SV%) in a 6-3 win over the Ottawa Senators. The Ducks enter Tuesday's game as -153 road favourites against a Vancouver Canucks team that has scored two or fewer goals in four of their last five (1-4-0).
